authoring_instructions:
MAIN EXACT PROMPT:
Revise the SECOND attached draft sprite atlas using the FIRST attached original portrait as the authoritative identity. Preserve original appearance, colors and equipment. Fully transparent RGBA, no backgrounds, text, grids or shadows. Exactly8 columns by8 rows with completely separate full bodies, equipment safely within each cell. Direction columns E right profile, SE front-right, S front toward viewer/down, SW front-left, W left profile, NW back-left, N fullback away/up, NE back-right. Rows1-2 idle,3-5 three distinct walk phases,6 attackwindup,7 contact,8 recovery. Every pose must be genuinely articulated and all 8 compass views distinct; no mirrored or repeated stills. Retain the narrow original crustacean identity, but change column1 to a TRUE RIGHT SIDE PROFILE and column5 to a TRUE LEFT SIDE PROFILE in all8 rows. A side view shows the side carapace and one near primary arm overlapping the farther arm, while diagonal views show more front breastplate. Column2 SE and column4 SW must remain clearly front-diagonal, not duplicates of E/W. Preserve the complete curved plated back for rear directions. Match the original soft shaded painted sprite style, avoid thick cartoon outlines. Original identity: The original CRABMAN is the narrow upright lobster/crab humanoid in the portrait, with pale salmon-pink/copper segmented chitin, white shell highlights, a curved hunched head/upper carapace, elongated plated body tapering downward, thin supporting legs and two long hooked claw forearms. Preserve this slim shrimp-like upright silhouette and its original number/shape of limbs; do not replace it with a broad sideways beach crab, add a human face, armor, clothes or weapons. Back directions show the curved ridged shell rather than its front. Walking has clearly articulated supporting legs and counter-moving claws. Attack brings the original claw arm back, reaches forward in the exact compass direction with the other arm still present, and recovers.
HIT/DEATH EXACT PROMPT:
Create the HIT/DEATH atlas for the FIRST attached ORIGINAL portrait. The second image only shows its draft movement design; keep the exact original identity and detailed painted 2D elevated RPG viewpoint, no cartoon outline or anatomy changes. Fully TRANSPARENT RGBA, no floor/shadows/text/grid/background/detached effects. EXACTLY8 COLUMNS and5 ROWS, forty separate complete articulated bodies. Keep each whole body AND weapon under45% of cell width/height, exceptionally generous clear gutters; nothing overlaps, touches or clips. Camera columns E right SIDE PROFILE, SE front-right, S straight FRONT looking toward viewer/down, SW front-left, W left SIDE PROFILE, NW back-left, N completely BACK away/up without face, NE back-right. Keep all8 compass views distinct while collapsing; E/W must not repeat the front-diagonal view. Rows: 1 pronounced HIT recoil,2 distinct HIT recovery,3 DEATH knees/legs buckle,4 collapsing very low onto ground,5 terminal entirely FLAT dead body. No extra rows. Each pose genuinely different through articulation, not translated/scaled duplicates. Keep every full silhouette connected. The original CRABMAN is the narrow upright lobster/crab humanoid in the portrait, with pale salmon-pink/copper segmented chitin, white shell highlights, a curved hunched head/upper carapace, elongated plated body tapering downward, thin supporting legs and two long hooked claw forearms. Preserve this slim shrimp-like upright silhouette and its original number/shape of limbs; do not replace it with a broad sideways beach crab, add a human face, armor, clothes or weapons. Back directions show the curved ridged shell rather than its front. Walking has clearly articulated supporting legs and counter-moving claws. Attack brings the original claw arm back, reaches forward in the exact compass direction with the other arm still present, and recovers. Recoil bends its segmented upper shell. Death buckles the legs, folds claws against the body and ends as a compact fully flat connected shell with curled limbs. No detached claws or disintegration.
